_doc: One file per place; see places_build.py. Amounts in kroner. The debt component, history and facts are refreshed by pipeline/fetch_eurostat.py from Eurostat tables gov_10q_ggdebt and demo_pjan; edit wording here, not numbers.
name: Denmark
title: Denmark National Debt Clock: Live Debt, Official Data
headline: central government debt
subject: The central government of Denmark
sum_note: Denmark central government gross debt (Maastricht definition, quarter-end), from Eurostat's quarterly government debt statistics, which are compiled from national data. The closest EU-comparable measure to the US Total Public Debt Outstanding.
scope_note: This is central government gross debt in the EU's Maastricht (excessive deficit procedure) definition, taken from Eurostat's quarterly table: everything the central government sector owes in currency and deposits, debt securities and loans, at nominal value and before subtracting any cash or other assets.  It is the closest EU-comparable match to the US national debt clock's Total Public Debt Outstanding. Figures are in kroner. Eurostat publishes it by sector, so the general government total is shown below as a fact.
trend_why: We use the latest four quarters rather than the last quarter because quarter-to-quarter changes swing with bond issuance calendars and short-term borrowing.
legend: Denmark's government debt is reported quarterly, at quarter-end. Issuance happens in lumps at auctions and maturities, so the live number is a straight-line projection between official quarter-end figures, shown here next to them.
cadence: Quarterly. Eurostat publishes each quarter-end figure (table gov_10q_ggdebt) about three months after the quarter ends.
after_text: , about three months after each quarter-end
next_update: The Q3 2026 quarter-end figure is expected from Eurostat roughly three months after the quarter ends; this page re-bases to it automatically on the next daily build after it appears.

components.includes: Central government gross debt at nominal value in the EU's Maastricht (EDP) definition: currency and deposits, short- and long-term debt securities and loans. In Denmark this is the central government (the State and the central-government bodies classified with it); the municipalities and regions are separate sectors.

facts.label: Denmark general government gross debt (Maastricht)
facts.note: All levels of government (central, state, local and social security) in the same Eurostat table, the measure used in EU fiscal rules. It covers more levels of government than the one ticking on this page. A year earlier (2025-06-30) it was kr884.9 billion. Central government is 75.4% of it.
facts.source_locator: geo=DK, sector S13, na_item GD, unit MIO_NAC

extra_sources.name: Eurostat, Government finance statistics - quarterly data

notes: Why Eurostat: it is the official EU statistical office and publishes quarterly government debt for every member state on one definition, compiled from the figures the national statistical institutes and central banks report to it. The fetcher reads its public API directly.
Provisional data: Eurostat flags the latest quarters as provisional and revises them in later releases. The page re-bases to each new release.

Why central government: the US clock ticks the federal Treasury's gross debt. The central government sector (Eurostat code S.1311) is the nearest match; state, local and social security debt are not in it. The table's breakdown by instrument adds up to the headline.

Currency: Denmark reports to Eurostat in kroner (million DKK, national currency, as published in table gov_10q_ggdebt, unit MIO_NAC). The world page converts to US dollars at the ECB's daily reference rate for DKK.
Cross-check: Danmarks Nationalbank publishes Danish central government debt on a national basis. National figures can differ from the Maastricht central government sector used here.
